subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw allow third-party plugin manifests to request install-time config mutations, and if so what allowed paths, confirmation, conflict/array behavior, provenance, and uninstall guidance are required?
rationale: This changes plugin install from enabling package metadata to mutating persisted user configuration, including security-sensitive provider/tool/auth-adjacent paths, so automation cannot safely choose the trust boundary or UX contract.

options.title: Define guarded config intent
options.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

options.title: Keep manual setup for now
options.body: Reject manifest-driven config writes and keep plugins using docs, setup flows, provider auth, or explicit `openclaw config patch` commands until a safer contract is designed.

options.title: Gate through ClawHub trust
options.body: Require ClawHub/package trust metadata or a plugin setup flow before core accepts install-time config mutation requests from manifests.

recommendation.title: Define guarded config intent
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: They posted the clearest existing product/security review on this issue and have recent plugin manifest/install documentation history.
